title: Build the Enterprise Facilities agent, end to end
reference: Building Agentic AI Solution on AWS Bedrock: a reference architecture (13 layers)

layers.title: Foundation Models via Bedrock
aws: Amazon Bedrock: Converse, InvokeModel, guardrails on model calls
layers.objective: Call a foundation model from code, the way every other layer will: a chat turn, a tool-use turn, and an embedding.
concepts: Converse API: one request shape for any chat model
Tool use: the model asks, your code runs the tool
Embeddings via InvokeModel
Model catalogue vs. the model id your code uses
you_build: List the models the account can use.
Send a Converse request and read the text and the token usage.
Send a Converse request with a toolConfig and handle stopReason.
Ask for an embedding with InvokeModel.
Attach the guardrail (layer 2) to a Converse call and watch it block a prompt attack.

provides: a working model client other layers import (chat, tool use, embeddings)

checks: Converse with toolConfig returns tool_use or end_turn
simplified: Answers come from one small local open model, not the vendor model; quality is far lower than the real Claude or Nova.
The standard Bedrock model ids resolve as compatibility aliases so unmodified code works.

layers.title: AgentCore Runtime
layers.objective: Host a supervisor agent that routes work to Facilities, Maintenance and Analytics sub-agents, one isolated session at a time.
concepts: Supervisor and sub-agents: plan, route, synthesise
The agent harness: step, token and cost budgets, checkpoints, timeouts and a kill switch
Session isolation: one agent process per session
Agent code is just code: package it, deploy it, invoke it
you_build: Write the supervisor and three sub-agents.
Package the agent code as a zip in S3.
CreateAgentRuntime named facilities-supervisor.
InvokeAgentRuntime with a session id and read the answer.
Invoke again with a second session id and prove the sessions do not share state.

provides: a runtime named facilities-supervisor that answers questions and routes to sub-agents
needs: layer 7 tools (reference tools until you build yours)

checks: CreateAgentRuntime facilities-supervisor exists and is READY
simplified: The simulator runs the agent code in its own sandbox; it does not run real AgentCore containers, and scaling and timeouts are not modelled.

layers.title: Tools (AWS Lambda)
layers.objective: Build the tools the agents call: read-only knowledge and asset lookups first, and write-capable tools that sit behind approval.
concepts: Tools are functions with a clear input and output contract
Read-only tools vs approval-gated write tools
Tool code reads data, never trusts the caller
you_build: Create the DynamoDB tables for assets, work orders and the approval ledger and seed a few rows.
Deploy a kb-search tool.
Deploy an asset-status tool that reads DynamoDB.
Deploy request-approval and create-work-order (write) tools.
Invoke each tool with lambda:Invoke and check the result.

provides: tool functions: kb-search, asset-status, request-approval, create-work-order
needs: layer 6 retrieval for kb-search (reference until you build it)

checks: write tools do not run without approval wiring
simplified: Lambda code runs in a simulator sandbox with the real SDKs; cold starts, memory limits and concurrency are not modelled.

layers.title: Knowledge Processing Pipeline
layers.objective: Turn documents into searchable knowledge: upload, extract, chunk, embed and index, and re-index automatically when a new document lands.
concepts: Chunking and why chunk size matters
Embeddings and vector search
Event-driven ingestion: S3 event, Lambda, ingestion job
Guardrail scan on documents before indexing
you_build: Upload SOPs and manuals to the facilities-docs bucket.
Create a vector collection and the knowledge base facilities-kb.
Create an S3 data source with fixed-size chunking.
Start an ingestion job and wait for COMPLETE.
Wire an S3 event to a Lambda that starts a new ingestion job.

provides: knowledge base facilities-kb filled from facilities-docs

checks: a new upload triggers a new ingestion job
simplified: Embeddings come from a small local model; retrieval quality is far lower than production models.
The vector store is a lightweight engine behind the same API.

layers.title: Knowledge Search Layer (RAG)
aws: Bedrock Knowledge Bases Retrieve and Rerank
layers.objective: Retrieve the right passages for a question, rank them, and keep the source location so answers can cite it.
concepts: Vector retrieval vs hybrid retrieval
Metadata filtering and access-aware search
Reranking
Why sources must travel with results
you_build: Call Retrieve for a boiler question and check the boiler SOP ranks first.
Call Retrieve for an air-handler question and check the manual ranks first.
Read the source location from each result.
Call Rerank on a result set.

provides: a retrieval function returning ranked passages with sources

checks: Retrieve ranks the boiler SOP first
Retrieve ranks the HVAC manual first for an AHU question
simplified: Ranking quality depends on a small local embedding model; BM25 hybrid search is limited.

layers.title: Response Generation
layers.objective: Answer in plain language from the retrieved documents, with citations, and filter personal data out before the user sees it.
concepts: Grounding: answer only from retrieved text
Citations and how to check them
Output guardrails: PII anonymisation and policy filters
you_build: Generate an answer from retrieved passages and attach citations.
Run the answer through the output guardrail.
Check that a planted phone number or email is masked.
Try RetrieveAndGenerate as a one-call alternative.

provides: a function that returns a grounded, cited, filtered answer

checks: PII is masked in the output
RetrieveAndGenerate returns an answer with citations
simplified: Guardrails are deterministic simple filters, not the vendor's trained classifiers.
Answer quality is that of a small local model.

layers.title: AgentCore Memory
layers.objective: Give the agent memory: short-term events within a session and long-term records it can retrieve later.
concepts: Short-term memory: the events of one session
Long-term memory: records that outlive a session
Scoping by user and tenant; retention and poisoning risks
you_build: CreateMemory named facilities-memory.
Create events for a user and an assistant turn in a session.
List the events to replay the session.
Retrieve long-term memory records for a user.

provides: memory facilities-memory with events and retrievable records

simplified: Long-term extraction is simplified; no vendor memory-extraction model.

layers.title: AgentCore Gateway
layers.objective: Put one governed door in front of the tools: a tool catalogue, schema validation, and a policy check on every call.
concepts: Tool catalogue over MCP
Policy on every tool call: identity, role, attributes
Schema validation and request throttling
Audit with the user's identity
you_build: CreateGateway named facilities-gateway and wait for READY.
Add the Lambda tools as a gateway target.
List tools over MCP (tools/list).
Call a tool over MCP (tools/call).
Create a policy engine with a Cedar policy that allows read-only tools only.

provides: a gateway facilities-gateway exposing the tools over MCP with a policy

checks: a policy engine with a Cedar policy exists
simplified: Cedar policy evaluation in the simulator is simplified; check which policy features are enforced before relying on them.

layers.title: Actions and Approval
layers.objective: Make write actions safe: classify risk, park the action for a human, record every decision, and only then execute.
concepts: Risk levels: low auto-approves, medium and high need a human
Durable approval state: the workflow waits for a callback
An approval ledger as the system of record
Idempotency and rollback
you_build: Create the state machine work-order-approval with a waitForTaskToken step.
Make the agent produce an approval request and check the execution is RUNNING and the ledger shows PENDING.
Check no work order exists before approval.
Approve with SendTaskSuccess and see the work order created.
Reject with SendTaskFailure and see nothing written.

provides: an approval workflow and ledger: nothing is written until a human approves

checks: a request parks as RUNNING and PENDING
simplified: Step Functions callback semantics are modelled; timeouts and service quotas are not.

layers.title: Access and Perimeter Security
layers.objective: Sign users in, carry their identity to every layer, and put a protected edge in front of the tools.
concepts: User pools, sign-in and tokens
A JWT authorizer on the API
Rate-based WAF rules
you_build: CreateUserPool facilities-users and a client.
Create a user and sign in to get a JWT.
Call GetUser with the access token.
Create a WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule.
Create a REST API with a /search route that needs the token.

provides: a user pool and an edge that only lets signed-in users reach the tools

checks: a web ACL with a rate rule exists
the API route needs the token
simplified: Tokens are real signed JWTs, but account recovery, MFA and federation are simplified.

layers.title: Channels and Interface
layers.objective: Let people reach the agent through web, mobile, chat or API, filter what comes in, and tell approvers what is waiting.
concepts: Input guardrails: prompt attacks and denied words
The approver inbox: topic fan-out to a queue
you_build: CreateGuardrail facilities-guardrail and a version.
Check a normal question passes.
Check a prompt injection is blocked.
Check a denied word is blocked.
Create the approver-inbox topic and a queue subscribed to it.

provides: guardrail facilities-guardrail and the approver inbox

checks: a message to the topic reaches the queue
simplified: Guardrails are deterministic simple filters, not the vendor's trained classifiers.

layers.title: AgentOps and Observability
layers.objective: See what the agent did: traces for every step, metrics for KPIs, structured logs tied to the trace, and evaluations.
concepts: Spans per agent and per tool
Metrics and logs correlated by trace id
Evaluators for answer quality
you_build: Send one trace segment per agent and tool span.
Read the trace back.
Put KPI metrics and list them.
Write structured logs with the trace id and read them back.
List the available evaluators.

provides: an observable agent: traces, metrics and logs you can query

checks: trace segments can be read back
logs round-trip with the trace id
simplified: Trace and metric storage is simplified; canary and rollback workflow are not simulated.

layers.title: Governance and Security
layers.objective: Protect and audit the whole app: encrypt the sensitive records, and prove who did what.
concepts: Envelope protection with an encryption context
SSE-KMS on stored objects
An audit trail of approval events
you_build: Create a KMS key with an alias and rotation.
Encrypt and decrypt an approval record with an encryption context.
Write an object with SSE-KMS.
Create a trail, start logging, and find the approval events in the trail.

provides: a key and an audit trail covering the approval path

checks: encrypt and decrypt round-trip with the context
CloudTrail lookup shows the approval events
simplified: IAM policy evaluation is simplified; check the capability notes for what is enforced.
